scope: Curated starting map, not exhaustive. Inspection levels are explicit.

sources.title: Gaussian elimination is not optimal
sources.annotation: The seven-product construction starts the subcubic recursion approach. This is a finite algorithm, unlike an existence-only exponent statement.

sources.title: Relations between exact and approximate bilinear algorithms. Applications
sources.inspection: Bibliographic entry and use in OAI26
sources.annotation: Interpolation connects approximate bilinear constructions to exact asymptotic algorithms. The original article was not reviewed in full during initialization.

sources.title: Partial and total matrix multiplication
sources.inspection: Bibliographic entry and use in OAI26
sources.annotation: The asymptotic sum inequality connects simultaneous independent matrix products to exponent bounds.

sources.title: Relative bilinear complexity and matrix multiplication
sources.inspection: Bibliographic entry and use in OAI26
sources.annotation: A foundational source for the tensor-power and laser-method framework.

sources.title: The asymptotic spectrum of tensors
sources.inspection: Bibliographic entry and use in OAI26
sources.annotation: Spectral points encode asymptotic tensor comparisons through additive, multiplicative, monotone numerical invariants.

sources.title: Matrix multiplication via arithmetic progressions
sources.inspection: Bibliographic entry and use in OAI26
sources.annotation: Auxiliary tensors and progression-free sets underpin the later Coppersmith-Winograd tensor analyses.

sources.title: On the complexity of matrix multiplication
sources.annotation: A doctoral thesis on higher-power analysis. The thesis itself was not reviewed in full during initialization.

sources.title: Multiplying matrices faster than Coppersmith-Winograd
sources.inspection: Bibliographic entry and historical discussion in OAI26
sources.annotation: A higher-power analysis in the classical exponent-improvement sequence.
sources.version_note: OAI26 also cites the expanded corrected author version, dated July 1, 2014.

sources.title: Fast Matrix Multiplication
sources.annotation: A self-contained entry point for bilinear algorithms, tensors, and historical methods. It predates the later records.
sources.version_note: Theory of Computing Graduate Surveys 5; DOI 10.4086/toc.gs.2013.005.

sources.title: Powers of Tensors and Fast Matrix Multiplication
sources.annotation: Convex optimization of tensor-power analysis gives omega < 2.3728639.

sources.title: A Refined Laser Method and Faster Matrix Multiplication
sources.annotation: A refined component-extraction analysis gives omega < 2.37286.
sources.version_note: Preprint 2020; SODA 2021; TheoretiCS journal version 2024, DOI 10.46298/theoretics.24.21.

sources.title: Faster Matrix Multiplication via Asymmetric Hashing
sources.annotation: Combination-loss analysis and asymmetric hashing give omega < 2.371866.
sources.version_note: Preprint 2022; v5 November 28, 2023; FOCS 2023.

sources.title: New Bounds for Matrix Multiplication: from Alpha to Omega
sources.annotation: Further analysis gives omega <= 2.371552 and improvements for rectangular products.
sources.version_note: Preprint July 2023; SODA 2024.

sources.title: More Asymmetry Yields Faster Matrix Multiplication
sources.inspection: Primary abstracts, version history, and publisher metadata
sources.annotation: The pre-Dupont analysis gives omega < 2.371339. Later numerical improvements must be credited separately.
sources.version_note: v2 October 20, 2024; SODA 2025. v3 August 19, 2026 incorporates the 2.371177 bound credited to DUP26.

sources.title: Improving the matrix multiplication exponent with modern optimization and AlphaEvolve
sources.annotation: Optimization within the combination-loss framework yields omega < 2.371177. The paper includes rigorous certification of the numerical bound.
sources.version_note: Submitted August 17, 2026. This is the pre-9/4 comparison bound, not the current listed record.

sources.title: An Upper Bound of 9/4 for the Matrix Multiplication Exponent
sources.inspection: Primary TeX inspected; matching PDF pages visually inspected
sources.annotation: The complex-field 9/4 theorem uses shared-leg separation, convolution inequalities, and a discrete-growth argument. This is external work.
sources.version_note: Paper dated October 2, 2026. Inspected TeX Git blob: 4492e66c707b9329f763c46e7cc113ff21d2edc0. Main-branch links can change.

sources.title: Rectangular matrix multiplication from polynomial products
sources.annotation: The rectangular curve gives alpha >= 1/2 and returns 9/4 at the square shape. It does not lower the square exponent.
sources.version_note: v1 October 7, 2026 had the title Rectangular matrix multiplication from shared-leg entropy. v2 October 11. Author discloses GPT-6.1/Codex derivation and his review/responsibility.

sources.title: Polynomial Separation of a Shared Tensor Leg and Matrix Multiplication in Arbitrary Characteristic
sources.annotation: Polynomial separation uses M+n-1 source copies; n=M gives 2M-1 rather than 5M. It retains the 9/4 exponent.
sources.version_note: Manuscript dated October 9, 2026; submitted October 12. Enough distinct field elements are required before extension to an algebraic closure.

sources.title: Universal points in the asymptotic spectrum of tensors
sources.annotation: Constructs universal spectral points and relates tensor asymptotics to quantum functionals.

sources.title: A group-theoretic approach to fast matrix multiplication
sources.annotation: Embeds matrix multiplication into group algebras. This is an alternative construction framework, not a proof that omega equals two.

sources.title: Fast Matrix Multiplication: Limitations of the Laser Method
sources.annotation: Proves limitations for specified laser-method analyses. Such limitations are not lower bounds on unrestricted matrix multiplication.
sources.version_note: Preprint November 2014; conference publication 2015.

sources.title: Limits on the Universal Method for Matrix Multiplication
sources.annotation: The universal method on Coppersmith-Winograd tensors cannot yield an exponent below 2.16805. The tensor and method restrictions are essential.
sources.version_note: Preprint 2018; CCC 2019, DOI 10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2019.12.

sources.title: On cap sets and the group-theoretic approach to matrix multiplication
sources.inspection: Primary abstract and author archive metadata
sources.annotation: Cap-set and slice-rank methods obstruct the omega=2 route through abelian groups of bounded exponent in the specified framework.
sources.version_note: Preprint 2016; publication 2017.

sources.title: Matrix multiplication via matrix groups
sources.annotation: Investigates matrix-group constructions and limitations, including continuous analogues.
sources.version_note: Preprint 2022; ITCS 2023, DOI 10.4230/LIPIcs.ITCS.2023.19.

sources.title: Discovering faster matrix multiplication algorithms with reinforcement learning
sources.annotation: AlphaTensor searches for finite bilinear algorithms. A small-tensor improvement or hardware benchmark is not automatically an asymptotic exponent record.
sources.version_note: Nature 610, 47-53. Full author list is available at the source; the bibliography uses et al.

sources.title: Matrix multiplication over arbitrary fields
authors: GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol (disclosed proof generation)
sources.inspection: Repository README and disclosed verification record
sources.annotation: Extends the OpenAI theorem to every field using characteristic-sensitive separation and fixed-overhead descent. External authors report Lean verification.
sources.version_note: Upstream baseline adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a. Archived release DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23219128. No local rebuild here.

sources.title: Rectangular matrix multiplication over arbitrary rings: exponent 9/4
sources.annotation: Extends the rectangular curve to associative rings, including noncommutative and nonunital rings. It explicitly credits UZ26 for the curve.
sources.version_note: Inspected README blob f9fc18814ac14dc41cfb5785b439b30f9a910d21. Reported publication check October 14, 2026. No local Lean rebuild.

sources.title: Matrix multiplication from block identities
authors: Yuval Filmus repository; consult source for contribution details
sources.annotation: Gives a block-identities route with square and rectangular formalizations over every field. It reuses identified Navot/OpenAI APIs and credits UZ26.
sources.version_note: Inspected README blob 06cab6441f44afd899d7e7586f3134abdf20ff71. Formal polynomial and finite-field functional correctness are distinguished. No local Lean rebuild.

sources.title: Big O Speedrun: Matrix Multiplication
sources.annotation: Lists OpenAI at 2.25 with a Lean Verified label. This is a status source, not an independent proof by this repository.
sources.version_note: Data updated October 20, 2026 at 9:17 AM PT; site says its proof check was October 10 at 10:45 PM PT.
